content:
Hi all, I have a branch on my fork that defines linear means and uses them to prove Jensen's inequality (and also conditional Jensen's inequality). I don't think this is too well known so I'll explain a bit.

A (isotonic) linear mean is map M : (E → R) → R that is linear on a submodule L of E → R with some additional properties:

  • we want M to be monotone on L (this is the isotonic part)
  • 1 ∈ L
  • M 1 = 1 i.e. M is normalized (though I think this property may be better suited as a typeclass)

A prototypical example is M f := ∫ x, f x ∂μ and L := { f | Integrable f μ } where μ is a probability measure.

Jessen was able to generalize Jensen's inequality on ℝ to this setting. Later, McShane generalized this to work on Banach space B by defining what I call an "extended linear mean". (In fact, I pretty much made up every name other than "linear mean".) An extended linear mean is a linear mean with another function ℳ : (E → B) → B and domain ℒ : Set (E → B)where the only condition is that the two means have to be compatible with continuous linear maps, i.e. for all l : B →L[R] R and f ∈ ℒ, l ∘ f ∈ L and M (l ∘ f) = l (ℳ f). Continuing with the above example, we have ℳ f := ∫ x, f x ∂μ and ℒ := { f | Integrable f μ } where now, f : E → B.

McShane's generalization states that for R := ℝ and under certain conditions (basically geometric Hahn-Banach) on B, if s : Set B is closed, φ : B → ℝ is continuous and convex on s, f ∈ ℒ, φ ∘ f ∈ L and ∀ x, f x ∈ s, then φ (ℳ f) ≤ M (φ ∘ f). Using the example I gave, this is almost exactly docs#Convex.integral_mem. (To make it exactly Jensen's inequality, we need to add an extra assumption involving what I called the "conegligible filter" on E, which corresponds to ae μ. I won't say more in this message though.) Guseinov was able to drop the closed condition on s when the vector span of s is finite dimensional which I have also formalized (and you may know this to be true for Jensen's inequality for expected values).

I was able to generalize this concept of (extended) linear means to "conditional (extended) linear means" which covers conditional expectation and conditional Jensen's inequality (docs#ConvexOn.map_condExp_le). Here M has type (E → R) → (E → R) instead. Doing this needed a bit more definitions and you can see the exact statement in by branch. (On a side note: I haven't been able to generalize the finite dimensional version despite it being apparently being true for the conditional expectation. I suspect there would need to be many more conditions on the mean function...)

I think linear means should be in mathlib, and you can also state power means and Holder's inequality using them though I haven't formalized any of that yet. I'm not sure if "conditional linear means" are worth adding just because the only (non-trivial) example I know is the conditional expectation (and tbh also because I just made up the definition). Anyways, I haven't contributed a new definition + corresponding API before so I would love feedback + thoughts on this. There's no PR yet but I really hope you all think this is worth adding!
